gaps.concept: Syncytiotrophoblasts secrete hCG, which acts like LH to maintain the corpus luteum and its progesterone secretion.
gaps.why_tested: An early pregnancy stem asks which placental cell and hormonal action prevent corpus luteum regression. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: Pregnancy tests detect the β subunit of hCG; its α subunit is shared with LH, FSH, and TSH.
gaps.why_tested: A positive pregnancy test asks which hormone subunit provides specificity. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK704/)

gaps.concept: The luteal–placental progesterone shift occurs around gestational weeks 7–10; the placenta becomes the dominant source after week 10.
gaps.why_tested: A corpus luteum removal stem asks when placental progesterone can sustain pregnancy. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: Progesterone maintains the decidualized endometrium and inhibits myometrial contractions.
gaps.why_tested: An early pregnancy stem asks how progesterone supports implantation and uterine quiescence. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: Placenta lacks CYP17 activity and uses fetal adrenal DHEA-S to synthesize estrogens; fetal liver modification supplies estriol precursors.
gaps.why_tested: A fetoplacental steroid pathway asks why placental estrogen synthesis depends on the fetus. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: Estrogen promotes uterine enlargement and mammary duct growth; progesterone promotes mammary lobuloalveolar development.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnancy hormone stem asks which steroid drives each reproductive tissue change. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK559304/)

gaps.concept: High estrogen and progesterone suppress milk secretion despite rising prolactin; placental delivery removes this inhibition.
gaps.why_tested: A postpartum stem asks why copious milk secretion begins after delivery. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK148965/)

gaps.concept: Placental hPL promotes maternal lipolysis and free fatty acid use, sparing glucose for the fetus.
gaps.why_tested: A metabolic stem asks how maternal fuel use changes as fetal glucose demand increases. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: Maternal pancreatic β cells increase insulin secretion to compensate for pregnancy insulin resistance; fasting glucose tends to fall.
gaps.why_tested: A glucose tolerance stem contrasts normal pregnancy adaptation with gestational diabetes. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: hCG weakly stimulates TSH receptors, transiently lowering maternal TSH in the first trimester.
gaps.why_tested: An early pregnancy thyroid panel shows mildly suppressed TSH without primary hyperthyroidism. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK539766/)

gaps.concept: Free T4 remains approximately normal despite increased total T4 from estrogen-induced TBG.
gaps.why_tested: A thyroid panel asks whether increased total T4 indicates hyperthyroidism in pregnancy. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: Estrogen-driven lactotroph hyperplasia enlarges the pituitary, increasing susceptibility to ischemic necrosis after severe postpartum hemorrhage.
gaps.why_tested: Failure to lactate after hemorrhagic delivery points to Sheehan syndrome. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278962/)

gaps.concept: Renin and aldosterone rise despite lower blood pressure, promoting maternal sodium and water retention.
gaps.why_tested: A hormone panel asks why plasma volume expands during a vasodilated pregnancy. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK559304/)

gaps.concept: Increased blood flow can produce a benign systolic ejection murmur and S3 during pregnancy.
gaps.why_tested: An asymptomatic pregnant patient with a new systolic murmur asks whether it reflects normal physiology. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK539766/)

gaps.concept: Venous stasis from uterine compression adds to pregnancy-associated thrombosis risk.
gaps.why_tested: A venous thrombosis stem asks for a mechanical contributor beyond elevated clotting factors. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK559304/)

gaps.concept: Platelet counts may fall mildly in normal pregnancy because of hemodilution and increased consumption.
gaps.why_tested: A mildly low platelet count without bleeding or hypertension asks whether gestational thrombocytopenia is plausible. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK559304/)

gaps.concept: Physiologic dilutional anemia is usually normocytic; microcytosis with low ferritin suggests iron deficiency.
gaps.why_tested: A low hemoglobin stem asks which findings exceed expected plasma-volume dilution. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK557783/)

gaps.concept: Respiratory rate is usually unchanged; increased tidal volume raises minute ventilation.
gaps.why_tested: A pulmonary physiology stem asks which breathing variable accounts for increased ventilation. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK539766/)

gaps.concept: Renal plasma flow rises, serum BUN falls, and urinary protein excretion may physiologically approach 300 mg/day.
gaps.why_tested: A renal panel or urine collection asks which results can occur in an uncomplicated pregnancy. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK559304/)

gaps.concept: Placental alkaline phosphatase raises maternal serum alkaline phosphatase without implying liver injury.
gaps.why_tested: An otherwise normal liver panel shows isolated alkaline phosphatase elevation late in pregnancy. [Source](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/gynecology-and-obstetrics/approach-to-the-pregnant-woman-and-prenatal-care/physiology-of-pregnancy)

gaps.concept: Estrogen increases biliary cholesterol saturation, while progesterone reduces gallbladder motility, promoting gallstones.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnant patient with biliary colic asks for the hormonal mechanism behind gallstone risk. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK559304/)
